qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Local haul-radius quarry monopolies (low value-to-weight ratio limits truck transport to ~25-50 miles) and stringent local permitting barriers create an irreplaceable infrastructure moat. Pricing power has been demonstrated across three decades with uninterrupted positive annual aggregates pricing gains, including +10% in FY2024 ($21.80/ton) and +7% in FY2025 ($23.30/ton).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Peace-of-Mind Balance Sheet & Real Cash Conversion). Irreplaceable US Sunbelt quarry franchise with unassailable pricing power, but fails Gate 6 on excessive leverage (4.66x debt/NI at $5.29B debt vs $1.14B net income), heavy maintenance/growth capex absorption (multi-year FCF conversion 68.7% vs 80% hurdle), and sub-hurdle 8.4% 10-year median GAAP ROIC diluted by serial debt-funded acquisitions.
qualitative.evidence: Martin Marietta Materials (MLM) operates irreplaceable aggregates quarries across high-growth Sunbelt and non-residential hubs. While local haul-radius protection enables steady pricing power (aggregates ASP up 10% in FY2024 to $21.80/ton and up 6.9% in FY2025 to $23.30/ton), the business model fails Gate 6 criteria: (1) 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 8.41% (ranging from 7.9% to 10.1%, with FY2024's 15.4% distorted by a one-off divestiture gain of $2.1B South Texas cement assets to CRH); (2) Multi-year Free Cash Flow conversion is 68.69%, falling well short of the 80% hurdle due to intensive quarry stripping, equipment overhaul, and fleet replacement capex ($807M capex vs $637M D&A in FY2025); (3) Long-term debt stands at $5,293M against $1,137M net income and $67M cash, yielding a Net Debt / Net Income ratio of 4.60x (and Debt / NI of 4.66x), exceeding the <= 4.0x ceiling. Capital allocation under CEO Ward Nye has successfully shifted the portfolio toward pure-play aggregates, but ongoing debt-funded M&A keeps leverage structurally elevated.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
